candidates.title: The Second Heat
candidates.premise:
Theo Marek is twenty-six, has a chemistry degree he has never used, and pays his rent driving a forklift at a scrap yard. His real life is a hobby: nine years of arguing with strangers online about knife steel. He knows two things cold. Metal goes hard if you heat it and cool it fast. Hard metal snaps — unless you give it a second, gentler heat straight after, which leaves it hard and tough both.

Then he wakes up on a black beach called Sarrow, on a coast where people do all of that to their own bodies. Children are held in the smoke of the vent — a crack in the ground that breathes heat — and the ones it takes can turn parts of themselves hard as struck iron. They are known by how deep the change goes: hands, then arms, then all through, and past that a few who can turn it on and off inside a single punch. Hard men catch axes barehanded. They also shatter, because nobody here has ever thought to cool a man down slowly on purpose.

Theo can. Everyone else was set one way at seven and stayed that way; he arrived grown and unset, so he can go hard, bring himself back soft, and go hard again. It costs him. Every cycle kills the feeling in another patch of skin, and his body is slower to change each time. The other half of the coast works the opposite way — bending, never breaking — and one of their palms on a hard man's neck drains everything he has raised. They have noticed it does nothing to Theo. So has the house up the coast that collects the best men and does not send them back.

records.subject: sys_hard_side
records.value: system

records.subject: sys_hard_side
records.value: Heat goes into a body from the vent; how the body comes back down decides what it is made of. Come down fast and the part you cooled is hard as struck iron and brittle in the same breath. Hardness is a state you raise, hold, and lose, and raising it takes days. Every trip through the heat coarsens what you are made of, permanently, so the whole coast is spending a thing it cannot get back and everybody knows it.

records.subject: sys_hard_side
records.value: Seawater comes off a man in a sheet of steam; a tapped forearm rings like a pot; a clay cup comes apart in a hand that meant to be gentle.

records.subject: sys_hard_side
records.value: Skin to skin, cold wins. A soft-worker's palm drains a hard man to nothing in the time it takes to say his name, and no hard man has ever put anything into a soft body. A body is set at seven in the smoke and nothing has ever changed one back, so a child who wants the other side is out of luck by breakfast. What a hard man can do that a soft one never will: stand in a rockfall and walk out. What a soft-worker can do that a hard man never will: reach into the vent mouth and clear it, which is where all the heat the hard side lives on comes from. The two houses touch on purpose in exactly one place, the tide line on the black sand, where the callings are held and where every argument on this coast ends up.

records.subject: sys_hard_side_view
records.value: Seawater comes off a man in a sheet of steam; a tapped forearm rings like a pot; a clay cup comes apart in a hand that meant to be gentle.

records.value: Nobody can tell how many heats they have left. The coast counts the ones spent and guesses.

records.subject: rule_hot_then_cold_makes_hard
records.value: Heat a part of the body through and cool it fast, and that part goes hard as struck iron and stays hard until it is heated again — and it goes brittle in the same moment.

records.subject: rule_hot_then_cold_makes_hard
records.value: He comes out of the surf trailing steam and the caller taps his forearm and it rings.

records.subject: rule_hot_then_cold_makes_hard
records.value: A fight at Sarrow opens with hard men walking straight in, and is decided by whoever works out how to hit the same spot twice.

records.subject: rule_hot_then_cold_makes_hard
records.value: Nobody hard is handed a baby, a cup, or a rope, and no hard man takes offence at it.

records.subject: rule_hot_then_cold_makes_hard
records.value: The docks run on light gear and short ropes because two arm-deep men lift what a crane lifts, and nobody has built a crane here in forty years.

records.subject: rule_every_heat_coarsens
records.value: Every time a body is taken hot it comes back coarser — slower to harden, slower to soften, never fine again. A body holds a limited number of heats and nobody learns their own number until they spend the last one.

records.subject: rule_every_heat_coarsens
records.value: He counts out loud before he steps into the smoke, and every year the numbers come slower.

records.subject: rule_every_heat_coarsens
records.value: Houses spend their old men first and keep the young out of the smoke until a fight is certain, which is why the young ones are dangerous and stupid.

records.subject: rule_every_heat_coarsens
records.value: A man who believes he is on his last heat says so out loud at the vent mouth, and everyone in hearing stops walking and stands still until he is finished.

records.subject: rule_every_heat_coarsens
records.value: Nobody on this coast marries before a man's fourth heat, because that is the first point he can guess what is left of him.

records.subject: rule_hard_feels_nothing
records.value: A hardened part feels nothing at all — not heat, not a cut, not weight, not grip.

records.subject: rule_hard_feels_nothing
records.value: He lifts a clay cup, it comes apart in his fingers, and he stands there looking at the pieces.

records.subject: rule_hard_feels_nothing
records.value: Nobody here questions a hard man with pain; they hold him in cold water until he is soft enough to feel something.

records.subject: rule_hard_feels_nothing
records.value: Hard men eat with their hands and drink from wood, and the taverns at Sarrow own no crockery.

records.subject: rule_hard_feels_nothing
records.value: They come off a burning deck cooked through the back and find out when somebody tells them.

records.subject: rule_a_body_is_set_once
records.value: At seven a child is held in the vent smoke, and whichever way the body goes — hard or soft — is the way it goes for the rest of its life. Nobody has ever changed.

records.subject: rule_a_body_is_set_once
records.value: The child comes out coughing, somebody says 'soft', and the mother's hands go still on her knees.

records.subject: rule_a_body_is_set_once
records.value: Smoke morning is the only day this coast keeps; families walk down the black sand before light and nobody speaks on the way back up.

records.subject: rule_a_body_is_set_once
records.value: A hard family that gets a soft child walks it to the tide house before noon, and in two hundred years the houses have never once argued about one.

records.subject: rule_a_body_is_set_once
records.value: A man states his side before he states his case, because it decides who is allowed to put a hand on whom.

records.value: criterion

records.value: ordinal

records.subject: hand_deep
records.value: Both hands stay a dull brown-grey for a day after a heat, and the caller's rod rings clean off the knuckles and dead off the wrist.

records.subject: hand_deep
records.value: One full heat in the smoke and two days of shaking so hard you cannot hold a spoon, with somebody sitting on you so you do not fall in the fire.

records.subject: hand_deep
records.value: Turn both hands hard for as long as you can hold a breath: catch a dropped blade by the edge, punch through a plank door, take a hammer on the palm.

records.subject: arm_deep
records.value: The colour comes up to the shoulders, and the caller walks the rod up the arm and it rings the whole way to the collarbone.

records.subject: arm_deep
records.value: Two heats inside one season and a quench in the winter surf, which stops the heart of about one man in nine; whoever pulls you out is somebody who now owns a piece of your life.

records.subject: arm_deep
records.value: Hard from fingertips to shoulders for a slow count of a hundred: turn an axe on your forearm, lift what four men lift, take a door off its hinges with a shove.

records.subject: all_through
records.value: The colour goes over the throat and face; the man's own footprints crack the boardwalk, so the coast lays sand paths for them.

records.subject: all_through
records.value: A heat held until you black out and somebody else decides when to pull you, plus the year afterwards of not being able to feel your own skin — and the far house comes and puts your name on a list of two.

records.subject: all_through
records.value: Hard everywhere at once: walk out of a rockfall, come off a burning deck, take a fall that kills and stand up asking what happened.

records.subject: quick_turn
records.value: Nothing shows at rest, and then it shows for half a second in exactly the spot being hit, like a coin of colour that arrives and goes.

records.subject: quick_turn
records.value: Four seasons of being struck on purpose, every day, by somebody who will not stop if you are wrong; and the coarsening that comes with it takes your speed of change down for the rest of your life.

records.subject: quick_turn
records.value: Move at full speed and harden only the part being struck, at the moment it is struck: nothing lands, and you are never the slow heavy thing a hard man usually is.

records.subject: made_over
records.value: The hand changes shape in front of people — an edge, a hook, a flat — and holds it, and the colour that comes up is one nobody else's skin makes.

records.subject: made_over
records.value: A heat taken past the point where the body should stop working, brought back down over a night by hand, alone, because nobody else can do it for you; those who fail come apart and are swept up.

records.subject: made_over
records.value: Change what parts of you are made of at will: grow an edge out of the forearm, make a bone springy enough to bend instead of break, and close a break in yourself by re-forming it.

records.subject: sys_soft_side
records.value: system

records.subject: sys_soft_side
records.value: Heat taken slowly and let go slowly does not harden a body, it opens it: the body bends where it would break and passes heat through itself instead of holding it. The same slowness undoes hardness wherever it finds it, in yourself or in somebody else, which makes a soft-worker the one thing on this coast a hard man cannot simply walk through.

records.subject: sys_soft_side
records.value: She lifts a bar off the sand still glowing, keeps it rolling across her palms the whole way down the beach, sets it in the water, and her hands are pink and not burnt.

records.subject: sys_soft_side
records.value: The soft side owns the vent mouth, because only a soft-worker can go into a crack that would cook anyone else and clear what has fallen into it. Every heat the hard side climbs on comes out of a hole that the other house keeps open, and the day the tide house walks away from the vent for a month, nobody climbs at all.

records.subject: sys_soft_side_nature
records.value: The tide house has known for three generations that it holds the hard side by the throat and has never once said so out loud.

records.subject: rule_slow_heat_makes_bend
records.value: Heat taken in slowly and let go slowly makes a body bend instead of break, for as long as it keeps moving.

records.subject: rule_slow_heat_makes_bend
records.value: She goes through a gap a hand's width narrower than she is and comes out the far side unbruised, still talking.

records.subject: rule_slow_heat_makes_bend
records.value: Soft-workers carry the injured and the newborn, and every birth on the coast has one in the room.

records.subject: rule_slow_heat_makes_bend
records.value: They are put where the line is expected to fold, because a folding line with soft-workers in it does not come apart.

records.subject: rule_slow_heat_makes_bend
records.value: The vent mouth is cleared by people who go through gaps narrower than their own shoulders, so nothing on this coast is built wide.

records.subject: rule_the_palm_takes_it_back
records.value: A soft-worker's bare hand on bare skin drains a hardened part back to nothing in about the time it takes to say the man's name. What was raised over days has to be raised again from the start.

records.subject: rule_the_palm_takes_it_back
records.value: A palm on the back of the neck, a sound like a kettle going quiet, and his knuckles stop ringing.

records.subject: rule_the_palm_takes_it_back
records.value: A soft-worker stands at every door where hard men are not to be let in hard, and touching one on the way past is how you agree to it.

records.subject: rule_the_palm_takes_it_back
records.value: No hard house has ever held a coast town without a tide house agreeing to it, and the agreements are made by two people on wet sand with nobody watching.

records.subject: rule_the_palm_takes_it_back
records.value: Anybody planning to take a hard man alive keeps a soft child on a rope, and that is the one thing this coast hangs people for.

records.subject: rule_soft_holds_the_heat_out
records.value: A soft-worker never stores heat; she moves it through and out, and can hold something that would take a hand off for exactly as long as she keeps it moving.

records.subject: rule_soft_holds_the_heat_out
records.value: She takes a glowing bar barehanded, keeps it turning across her palms the whole way, and sets it down without a mark on her.

records.subject: rule_soft_holds_the_heat_out
records.value: Everything hot on this coast — the vent mouth, the boiling shallows, the smoke hoods — is worked by one house, and the other house cannot do any of it.

records.subject: rule_soft_holds_the_heat_out
records.value: The tide house sets when the smoke runs and how long, and it has never had to raise its voice about it.

records.subject: rule_soft_holds_the_heat_out
records.value: A tide house can end a war on this coast by going home for a month, and has done it twice.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: agency

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: The crack under the coast that breathes heat, which is not alive and has moods anyway.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: Nothing. It breathes harder in some years than others and nobody has ever found out why.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: Everything anybody on this coast can do; when it is quiet, nobody climbs.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: Nothing and nobody, which is the part the coast cannot stand.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: It has been breathing weaker every season for six years, and every plan any house has is really a plan about that.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: White smoke coming up through black sand at low tide, and the sound of the shallows boiling three hundred paces out.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: Every rank in the house came out of it and the house has no other supply.

records.subject: the_vent_below
records.value: They are the only people who can reach into it, which is how they could do what they are doing.

records.subject: the_vent_below_belief
records.value: The coast's belief, not its own: that a man's conduct has anything to do with what the smoke does to him.

records.subject: the_vent_below_secret
records.value: It is not dying. Somebody has been opening a second mouth four days up the coast and the heat is going there.

records.subject: the_tap_rod
records.value: carrier

records.subject: the_tap_rod
records.value: A strip of moulted ash crab shell, a forearm long, that the caller runs up a man's arm at a calling.

records.subject: the_tap_rod
records.value: It rings clean off a part that is hard and dies flat off a part that is not, so the whole room hears exactly how deep a man goes.

records.subject: the_tap_rod
records.value: A rising series of clear notes up the forearm, and then one dull knock where the man stops.

records.subject: the_tap_rod
records.value: Whoever holds the rod says what a man is, and nobody has ever asked to hold it themselves.

records.subject: the_tap_rod_secret
records.value: Garran's rod-note now comes back low and even, which is a note this coast has never heard and has no name for.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: cast

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: A twenty-six-year-old from somewhere else, a chemistry graduate who drove a forklift and read about knife steel for nine years, now arm-deep on a coast that does it to people.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: To reach the far end of the change before his body stops changing.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: Explains things nobody asked about, in plain words, usually while doing something that should have his full attention.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: Sitting in hot sand with a hand on somebody's chest, watching the light on their skin and counting under his breath.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: She raised him three ranks in a year and has started asking how, in a tone he does not like.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: First man he ever brought back from cracked, and Garran now follows him around like a debt neither of them named.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: Bekk is faster, younger and correct that Theo has not earned a single thing he has.

records.subject: theo_marek
records.value: Her palm did nothing to him and she has not told her own house yet.

records.subject: theo_marek_belief
records.value: That he can keep the second heat quiet until he is high enough that it does not matter who knows.

records.subject: theo_marek_secret
records.value: He has counted his cycles and he thinks he has about eleven left. He has told no one, including himself, out loud.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: cast

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: The woman who runs the hard house at Sarrow, all-through, and by her own count on her second-to-last heat.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: To leave Sarrow with somebody standing in it who can hold it after her.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: Short sentences, no encouragement, and one question at the end that takes the skin off you.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: Everything she decides is decided by a woman who will not be here in two winters and knows it.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: Sits through the whole calling without getting up, because standing up is a heat she is not spending.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: She is the only reason the far house has taken one man from Sarrow instead of four.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: He does not know, and he brings her water every morning.

records.subject: oda_sarn
records.value: They meet on the tide line and neither house is told what was agreed.

records.subject: oda_sarn_belief
records.value: That the far house will honour the one-man arrangement it has kept for thirty years.

records.subject: oda_sarn_secret
records.value: She cracked Garran on purpose so the far house would not take him.

records.subject: bekk_haul
records.value: cast

records.subject: bekk_haul
records.value: Nineteen, hand-deep going on arm-deep, the fastest thing on the beach and the loudest.

records.subject: bekk_haul
records.value: To be called arm-deep at the same calling Theo is, so that nobody can say he came second.

records.subject: bekk_haul
records.value: Talks in challenges, even when he is agreeing with you.

records.subject: bekk_haul
records.value: Turns up wherever Theo is standing, holds out a forearm, and waits to be tapped.

records.subject: bekk_haul
records.value: He has worked out that Theo never shakes for two days afterwards and he wants to know why.

records.subject: bekk_haul
records.value: Oda will not put him in the smoke again and he goes anyway.

records.subject: bekk_haul_belief
records.value: That coarsening is something that happens to old men.

records.subject: bekk_haul_secret
records.value: He has already taken three heats this season, two of them alone at night, which is one more than a body his age survives twice.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: cast

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: Twenty-four, of the tide house, the palm that stands at the calling ground door.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: To find out what Theo is, before anybody in her own house does.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: Asks small polite questions that turn out later to have been the whole conversation.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: Every day she does not tell her house is a day she has chosen a side she is not allowed to have.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: Stands with her hands loose and open at every door, and men walk a wider line around her than they need to.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: She clears the vent mouth two mornings in ten and has seen what is being done to it.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: The two of them settle on wet sand what the two houses shout about on dry.

records.subject: nissa_vell
records.value: She has touched him four times now, each time with a different excuse.

records.subject: nissa_vell_secret
records.value: Her hand on him did nothing at all, and that has never happened, and she reported it as a success.

records.subject: garran_ott
records.value: cast

records.subject: garran_ott
records.value: A cracked man — all-through once, shattered in the surf two winters ago — who Theo walked back down through a low heat and who now rings low instead of dead.

records.subject: garran_ott
records.value: To be put back in the smoke, which everybody including Theo thinks will kill him.

records.subject: garran_ott
records.value: Cheerful about things that are not funny, and goes quiet whenever Oda comes into a room.

records.subject: garran_ott
records.value: Taps his own forearm with a knuckle in the middle of conversations, listening to the note.

records.subject: garran_ott
records.value: He is the living proof of the second heat, and he will show anybody who asks.

records.subject: garran_ott
records.value: Brings her water every morning and has never once asked who put him in the surf that day.

records.subject: garran_ott_secret
records.value: He can feel about a third of his own body and he lies about which third.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: institution

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: The hard house at Sarrow: a long shed of sand floors and smoke hoods where children are held, men are tapped, and the pit with the slaghound in it sits at the far end.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: To keep enough men to matter without spending the ones it has.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: Everything on the black beach and about a day's walk inland.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: Anybody who has been tapped and rung.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: The rod going up an arm in front of a room of people, and the whole room listening for where the note dies.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: One man a generation goes up the coast, and nobody has ever come back down it.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: Every heat it spends came out of a hole the other house keeps clear.

records.subject: long_fire_house
records.value: She is the house; when she goes, the arrangement with the far house goes with her.

records.subject: long_fire_house_secret
records.value: It has been failing for nine years and covers it by calling fewer men and calling them louder.

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: institution

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: The soft house, built low at the water line: the people who clear the vent, carry the injured, and stand at doors.

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: To go on being the only thing that keeps the coast's heat running, without anybody ever saying it out loud.

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: Every hot place on the coast, and every doorway with a hard man on the other side of it.

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: Anyone whose hands come out of heat pink instead of burnt.

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: Two of them walking into white smoke with rakes and coming out an hour later, sooty and unhurt, arguing about something domestic.

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: They could stop the climb of every hard man alive by staying home for a month.

records.subject: tide_house
records.value: They sent her to the calling ground door to watch the far house, and she has been watching Theo instead.

records.subject: tide_house_secret
records.value: They have been widening a second vent mouth four days up the coast for six years.

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: A hard house four days up the coast that comes down once a generation and takes the all-through men away.

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: Bodies that can stand hard for years without moving.

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: The whole coast; nobody has refused them and stayed a house.

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: Any man whose footprints crack a boardwalk.

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: Three people in grey coats standing at the back of a calling, saying nothing, writing nothing, leaving before the end.

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: They have taken one man from Sarrow every generation and are due.

records.subject: the_far_house
records.value: They have heard there is a man here who cannot be drained.

records.subject: the_far_house_belief
records.value: That Sarrow still has only one man worth coming for.

records.subject: the_far_house_secret
records.value: The men they take are set into the sea floor to hold a shaft open, and they stand there until their last heat.

records.subject: the_year_the_vent_slept
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_year_the_vent_slept
records.value: Nine winters ago, when the crack stopped breathing for a full year.

records.subject: the_year_the_vent_slept
records.value: Nobody climbed, two houses came apart, and every man over thirty on this coast has a hole in the middle of what he can do.

records.subject: the_year_the_vent_slept
records.value: Old men who are hand-deep at forty and do not explain it.

records.subject: the_year_the_vent_slept
records.value: She was the only one who kept climbing that year, which is a thing she has never accounted for.

records.subject: the_year_the_vent_slept_secret
records.value: It did not sleep. That was the year the tide house first got a rake into the upper crack.

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: creature

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: A hand-sized crab that lives in the boiling shallows at the vent mouth.

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: A dry clatter under the shallows, and a noise like a struck pot when somebody steps on one.

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: It moults in water hot enough to cook it and drops straight into the cold current underneath, so the new shell comes up hard the way a man does and stays that way.

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: They crowd wherever the vent runs into the sea and disappear entirely in any season the vent breathes weakly.

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: Common, and thinning out every year, which is the first thing anybody noticed.

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: The caller's rod is a strip of moulted shell, because nothing else rings true against a hard arm.

records.subject: ash_crab
records.value: They climb standing legs and grip, and cold water is the only thing that makes them let go.

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: creature

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: A dog-sized animal that dens inside the warm cracks and has gone hard all the way through.

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: A sound like gravel poured onto stone, and pieces of it left on the rock where it ran.

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: It lives in heat and never cools slowly, so it is hard everywhere and brittle everywhere, and it hunts by running into things.

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: Dens where nothing else can go; dies out entirely in any year the vent sleeps.

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: The hard house keeps one in a pit at the end of the shed and stands seven-year-olds in front of it on smoke morning, so they see what a body becomes when it never comes down slowly.

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: Charges in a straight line, breaks a leg off on the third or fourth charge, and keeps charging on what is left.

records.subject: slaghound
records.value: None. Nothing that never cools has ever learned anything.

records.subject: myst_why_theo_never_set
records.value: Setting happens in growing bone. It has nothing to do with the smoke choosing anybody; it is that a seven-year-old's body finishes forming around whichever way it went first. Theo arrived finished. Nobody here has ever put an adult in the smoke because nobody here has ever had an adult who had not already been.

report.title: The Second Heat
report.domain: Heat treatment of metal — what heating and cooling does to how hard, how brittle and how bendy a thing is. Fast cooling makes it hard and snappable; slow gentle reheating afterwards makes it hard and tough; slow heating and slow cooling makes it soft and bendy and wipes out whatever hardness was there; and every trip through the fire coarsens the material for good.

world.title: The Second Heat
world.domain: Heat treatment of metal — what heating and cooling does to how hard, how brittle and how bendy a thing is. world.progression_means: What a body is made of, how much of it can be changed at once, and how fast it can change back.
world.inversion: Nothing is inverted or removed. Every piece of furniture a reader came for is here — a house that teaches, a proving ground, a caller who says your name out loud, a rival, a monster in a pit. What is this world's own is the engine underneath it and the man it is happening to.
world.premise:
Theo Marek is twenty-six, has a chemistry degree he has never used, and pays his rent driving a forklift at a scrap yard. His real life is a hobby: nine years of arguing with strangers online about knife steel. He knows two things cold. Metal goes hard if you heat it and cool it fast. Hard metal snaps — unless you give it a second, gentler heat straight after, which leaves it hard and tough both.

Then he wakes up on a black beach called Sarrow, on a coast where people do all of that to their own bodies. Children are held in the smoke of the vent — a crack in the ground that breathes heat — and the ones it takes can turn parts of themselves hard as struck iron. They are known by how deep the change goes: hands, then arms, then all through, and past that a few who can turn it on and off inside a single punch. Hard men catch axes barehanded. They also shatter, because nobody here has ever thought to cool a man down slowly on purpose.

Theo can. Everyone else was set one way at seven and stayed that way; he arrived grown and unset, so he can go hard, bring himself back soft, and go hard again. It costs him. Every cycle kills the feeling in another patch of skin, and his body is slower to change each time. The other half of the coast works the opposite way — bending, never breaking — and one of their palms on a hard man's neck drains everything he has raised. They have noticed it does nothing to Theo. So has the house up the coast that collects the best men and does not send them back.

systems.name: The Hard Side
systems.logic: Heat goes into a body from the vent; how the body comes back down decides what it is made of. Come down fast and the part you cooled is hard as struck iron and brittle in the same breath. Hardness is a state you raise, hold, and lose, and raising it takes days. Every trip through the heat coarsens what you are made of, permanently, so the whole coast is spending a thing it cannot get back and everybody knows it.
systems.interface: Skin to skin, cold wins. A soft-worker's palm drains a hard man to nothing in the time it takes to say his name, and no hard man has ever put anything into a soft body. A body is set at seven in the smoke and nothing has ever changed one back, so a child who wants the other side is out of luck by breakfast. What a hard man can do that a soft one never will: stand in a rockfall and walk out. What a soft-worker can do that a hard man never will: reach into the vent mouth and clear it, which is where all the heat the hard side lives on comes from. The two houses touch on purpose in exactly one place, the tide line on the black sand, where the callings are held and where every argument on this coast ends up.
systems.manifests_as: Seawater comes off a man in a sheet of steam; a tapped forearm rings like a pot; a clay cup comes apart in a hand that meant to be gentle.
systems.view_withholds: Nobody can tell how many heats they have left. The coast counts the ones spent and guesses.

criterion.evaluates: How much of a body the change reaches, and how fast it can be turned on and off.

ranks.visible_form: Both hands stay a dull brown-grey for a day after a heat, and the caller's rod rings clean off the knuckles and dead off the wrist.
ranks.cost_to_reach: One full heat in the smoke and two days of shaking so hard you cannot hold a spoon, with somebody sitting on you so you do not fall in the fire.
ranks.grants: Turn both hands hard for as long as you can hold a breath: catch a dropped blade by the edge, punch through a plank door, take a hammer on the palm.

ranks.visible_form: The colour comes up to the shoulders, and the caller walks the rod up the arm and it rings the whole way to the collarbone.
ranks.cost_to_reach: Two heats inside one season and a quench in the winter surf, which stops the heart of about one man in nine; whoever pulls you out is somebody who now owns a piece of your life.
ranks.grants: Hard from fingertips to shoulders for a slow count of a hundred: turn an axe on your forearm, lift what four men lift, take a door off its hinges with a shove.

ranks.visible_form: The colour goes over the throat and face; the man's own footprints crack the boardwalk, so the coast lays sand paths for them.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A heat held until you black out and somebody else decides when to pull you, plus the year afterwards of not being able to feel your own skin — and the far house comes and puts your name on a list of two.
ranks.grants: Hard everywhere at once: walk out of a rockfall, come off a burning deck, take a fall that kills and stand up asking what happened.

ranks.visible_form: Nothing shows at rest, and then it shows for half a second in exactly the spot being hit, like a coin of colour that arrives and goes.
ranks.cost_to_reach: Four seasons of being struck on purpose, every day, by somebody who will not stop if you are wrong; and the coarsening that comes with it takes your speed of change down for the rest of your life.
ranks.grants: Move at full speed and harden only the part being struck, at the moment it is struck: nothing lands, and you are never the slow heavy thing a hard man usually is.

ranks.visible_form: The hand changes shape in front of people — an edge, a hook, a flat — and holds it, and the colour that comes up is one nobody else's skin makes.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A heat taken past the point where the body should stop working, brought back down over a night by hand, alone, because nobody else can do it for you; those who fail come apart and are swept up.
ranks.grants: Change what parts of you are made of at will: grow an edge out of the forearm, make a bone springy enough to bend instead of break, and close a break in yourself by re-forming it.

rules.rule: Heat a part of the body through and cool it fast, and that part goes hard as struck iron and stays hard until it is heated again — and it goes brittle in the same moment.

consequences.consequence: A fight at Sarrow opens with hard men walking straight in, and is decided by whoever works out how to hit the same spot twice.
Nobody hard is handed a baby, a cup, or a rope, and no hard man takes offence at it.
The docks run on light gear and short ropes because two arm-deep men lift what a crane lifts, and nobody has built a crane here in forty years.

rules.manifests_as: He comes out of the surf trailing steam and the caller taps his forearm and it rings.

rules.rule: Every time a body is taken hot it comes back coarser — slower to harden, slower to soften, never fine again. A body holds a limited number of heats and nobody learns their own number until they spend the last one.

consequences.consequence: Houses spend their old men first and keep the young out of the smoke until a fight is certain, which is why the young ones are dangerous and stupid.
A man who believes he is on his last heat says so out loud at the vent mouth, and everyone in hearing stops walking and stands still until he is finished.
Nobody on this coast marries before a man's fourth heat, because that is the first point he can guess what is left of him.

rules.manifests_as: He counts out loud before he steps into the smoke, and every year the numbers come slower.

rules.rule: A hardened part feels nothing at all — not heat, not a cut, not weight, not grip.

consequences.consequence: Nobody here questions a hard man with pain; they hold him in cold water until he is soft enough to feel something.
Hard men eat with their hands and drink from wood, and the taverns at Sarrow own no crockery.
They come off a burning deck cooked through the back and find out when somebody tells them.

rules.manifests_as: He lifts a clay cup, it comes apart in his fingers, and he stands there looking at the pieces.

rules.rule: At seven a child is held in the vent smoke, and whichever way the body goes — hard or soft — is the way it goes for the rest of its life. Nobody has ever changed.

consequences.consequence: Smoke morning is the only day this coast keeps; families walk down the black sand before light and nobody speaks on the way back up.
A hard family that gets a soft child walks it to the tide house before noon, and in two hundred years the houses have never once argued about one.
A man states his side before he states his case, because it decides who is allowed to put a hand on whom.

rules.manifests_as: The child comes out coughing, somebody says 'soft', and the mother's hands go still on her knees.

systems.name: The Soft Side
systems.logic: Heat taken slowly and let go slowly does not harden a body, it opens it: the body bends where it would break and passes heat through itself instead of holding it. The same slowness undoes hardness wherever it finds it, in yourself or in somebody else, which makes a soft-worker the one thing on this coast a hard man cannot simply walk through.
systems.interface: The soft side owns the vent mouth, because only a soft-worker can go into a crack that would cook anyone else and clear what has fallen into it. Every heat the hard side climbs on comes out of a hole that the other house keeps open, and the day the tide house walks away from the vent for a month, nobody climbs at all.
systems.manifests_as: She lifts a bar off the sand still glowing, keeps it rolling across her palms the whole way down the beach, sets it in the water, and her hands are pink and not burnt.
systems.hidden_personality: The tide house has known for three generations that it holds the hard side by the throat and has never once said so out loud.

criterion.evaluates: How long a soft-worker can keep heat moving through her body and out the other side before it starts staying in.

rules.rule: Heat taken in slowly and let go slowly makes a body bend instead of break, for as long as it keeps moving.

consequences.consequence: Soft-workers carry the injured and the newborn, and every birth on the coast has one in the room.
They are put where the line is expected to fold, because a folding line with soft-workers in it does not come apart.
The vent mouth is cleared by people who go through gaps narrower than their own shoulders, so nothing on this coast is built wide.

rules.manifests_as: She goes through a gap a hand's width narrower than she is and comes out the far side unbruised, still talking.

rules.rule: A soft-worker's bare hand on bare skin drains a hardened part back to nothing in about the time it takes to say the man's name. What was raised over days has to be raised again from the start.

consequences.consequence: A soft-worker stands at every door where hard men are not to be let in hard, and touching one on the way past is how you agree to it.
No hard house has ever held a coast town without a tide house agreeing to it, and the agreements are made by two people on wet sand with nobody watching.
Anybody planning to take a hard man alive keeps a soft child on a rope, and that is the one thing this coast hangs people for.

rules.manifests_as: A palm on the back of the neck, a sound like a kettle going quiet, and his knuckles stop ringing.

rules.rule: A soft-worker never stores heat; she moves it through and out, and can hold something that would take a hand off for exactly as long as she keeps it moving.

consequences.consequence: Everything hot on this coast — the vent mouth, the boiling shallows, the smoke hoods — is worked by one house, and the other house cannot do any of it.
The tide house sets when the smoke runs and how long, and it has never had to raise its voice about it.
A tide house can end a war on this coast by going home for a month, and has done it twice.

rules.manifests_as: She takes a glowing bar barehanded, keeps it turning across her palms the whole way, and sets it down without a mark on her.

cast.is_a: A twenty-six-year-old from somewhere else, a chemistry graduate who drove a forklift and read about knife steel for nine years, now arm-deep on a coast that does it to people.
cast.wants: To reach the far end of the change before his body stops changing.
cast.secret: He has counted his cycles and he thinks he has about eleven left. He has told no one, including himself, out loud.
cast.false_belief: That he can keep the second heat quiet until he is high enough that it does not matter who knows.
cast.voice_tag: Explains things nobody asked about, in plain words, usually while doing something that should have his full attention.
cast.manifests_as: Sitting in hot sand with a hand on somebody's chest, watching the light on their skin and counting under his breath.

relationships.note: She raised him three ranks in a year and has started asking how, in a tone he does not like.
First man he ever brought back from cracked, and Garran now follows him around like a debt neither of them named.
Bekk is faster, younger and correct that Theo has not earned a single thing he has.
Her palm did nothing to him and she has not told her own house yet.

cast.is_a: The woman who runs the hard house at Sarrow, all-through, and by her own count on her second-to-last heat.
cast.wants: To leave Sarrow with somebody standing in it who can hold it after her.
cast.secret: She cracked Garran on purpose so the far house would not take him.
cast.false_belief: That the far house will honour the one-man arrangement it has kept for thirty years.
cast.prices_the_present: Everything she decides is decided by a woman who will not be here in two winters and knows it.
cast.manifests_as: Sits through the whole calling without getting up, because standing up is a heat she is not spending.
cast.voice_tag: Short sentences, no encouragement, and one question at the end that takes the skin off you.

relationships.note: She is the only reason the far house has taken one man from Sarrow instead of four.

cast.is_a: Nineteen, hand-deep going on arm-deep, the fastest thing on the beach and the loudest.
cast.wants: To be called arm-deep at the same calling Theo is, so that nobody can say he came second.
cast.secret: He has already taken three heats this season, two of them alone at night, which is one more than a body his age survives twice.
cast.false_belief: That coarsening is something that happens to old men.

cast.wants: To find out what Theo is, before anybody in her own house does.
cast.secret: Her hand on him did nothing at all, and that has never happened, and she reported it as a success.
cast.prices_the_present: Every day she does not tell her house is a day she has chosen a side she is not allowed to have.
cast.manifests_as: Stands with her hands loose and open at every door, and men walk a wider line around her than they need to.
cast.voice_tag: Asks small polite questions that turn out later to have been the whole conversation.

relationships.note: She clears the vent mouth two mornings in ten and has seen what is being done to it.

cast.is_a: A cracked man — all-through once, shattered in the surf two winters ago — who Theo walked back down through a low heat and who now rings low instead of dead.
cast.wants: To be put back in the smoke, which everybody including Theo thinks will kill him.
cast.secret: He can feel about a third of his own body and he lies about which third.
cast.manifests_as: Taps his own forearm with a knuckle in the middle of conversations, listening to the note.
cast.voice_tag: Cheerful about things that are not funny, and goes quiet whenever Oda comes into a room.

institutions.is_a: The hard house at Sarrow: a long shed of sand floors and smoke hoods where children are held, men are tapped, and the pit with the slaghound in it sits at the far end.
institutions.wants: To keep enough men to matter without spending the ones it has.
institutions.secret: It has been failing for nine years and covers it by calling fewer men and calling them louder.

mysteries.question: Why did the smoke never set Theo one way, when it has set every person on this coast for two hundred years?
mysteries.answer: Setting happens in growing bone. It has nothing to do with the smoke choosing anybody; it is that a seven-year-old's body finishes forming around whichever way it went first. Theo arrived finished. Nobody here has ever put an adult in the smoke because nobody here has ever had an adult who had not already been.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Both houses, who believe the smoke decides and that the decision is about the person.

mysteries.question: Who put Garran in the surf the day he shattered?
mysteries.answer: Oda did, deliberately, the week before the far house came down, so that they would find nothing worth taking. She has been bringing him back one favour at a time ever since and he still hands her water every morning.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Garran, who believes he mistimed his own quench.

mysteries.question: How many heats does a body actually hold?
mysteries.answer: It was never a count of heats. It is the total time held hot. Theo's short cycles cost a fraction of one long climb, which is why he is rising fast — and it means the coast's whole method, one enormous heat held until a man blacks out, has been burning bodies four times faster than it needed to for two hundred years.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Everyone, who counts heats out loud and believes the number is fixed at birth.

mysteries.question: Why has the vent breathed weaker every season for six years?
mysteries.answer: The tide house has been opening a second mouth four days up the coast, on ground they own, so that when the hard houses finally cannot climb, the heat and everyone who needs it will already be standing on tide-house sand.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: The hard house, which believes the coast is simply going cold and that this is nobody's fault.

mysteries.question: What happens to the all-through men the far house takes away?
mysteries.answer: They are hardened and set into the sea floor to hold a shaft open against the water. They stand there, feeling nothing, until they spend their last heat, and the shaft is how the far house reaches the deep part of the crack that everybody else's vent is only a leak from.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Sarrow, which believes being taken is the honour at the top of everything.

directives.text: Fast and plain. The engine is never explained to the reader; it is demonstrated by somebody paying for it in the same scene.
Never use the words rank, level, tier, stage or standing. This coast says hand-deep, arm-deep, all-through, quick-turn, made-over, and says them out loud at callings.
Every rise in what Theo can do is preceded, in the same chapter or an earlier one, by a visible cost: a patch of skin he cannot feel, a day he cannot use an arm, a person who is now against him.
The first twelve scenes get Theo from arm-deep to the edge of all-through, put the second heat in front of witnesses at least twice, and end with the far house arriving early.
Callings are the world's set pieces: the rod, the note, the room listening for where it dies. Use one roughly every four scenes and never the same way twice.

candidates.title: The Root Decides
candidates.premise:
Sela Quen is twenty-two and spent four years on a rooftop in a river port breeding racing pigeons, because she liked it and there was nothing else to do up there. The hobby teaches exactly one thing: watch what a bird passes on to its young, not what the bird looks like standing in front of you.

Then she came downriver into the delta, where people join living things together. A grafter cuts a part off one animal and binds it onto another, and if the two are near enough kin it takes and grows: a hound with a second heart, a man with an arm that used to belong to a bear. How far apart the two can be is how a grafter is known — same flesh, then like flesh, then far flesh, and above those a handful of people alive who can join two things with no kinship at all. Sela is a like flesh, two steps up, and slower at it than most people her age.

Everything a grafter makes is barren. Joined creatures never have young, so a grafter's work dies when the grafter does, and the only people here who make anything that outlasts them are the breeders, who join nothing, and whose bodies refuse another creature's flesh so hard that a breeder's flat palm on a fresh join will open it up.

Sela's crosses have young. She does not know why yet. Halder Vone, the best breeder in the delta, has taken her into his own pens to prove she is lying — and if she turns out not to be, everything his family is rests on her being stopped.

records.subject: sys_grafting
records.value: A body will grow together with another living thing only if it takes that thing for near enough kin. The nearer the kin, the surer the hold; the further, the more of it sloughs away in the first season. Whatever is joined has one weak place forever, exactly where the two met. A new join knits over a season and only if somebody stays close enough to keep it warm, still and watched. The body underneath decides how big and how strong the whole thing is; the part added on decides what it can do. And nothing joined has young.

records.subject: sys_grafting
records.value: Palm to a fresh join and the join opens: refusal beats a take every time, and nothing a grafter makes has ever held on a breeder's body. Children are sorted at eight by pressing a scrap of another child's skin to the inside of a wrist for three days — it takes, or the wrist swells and goes hot — and afterwards you are on one side of the delta or the other for good. What a grafter can do that a breeder never will: put a dead thing's working part into a living body and have it working by morning. What a breeder can do that a grafter never will: make ten of something, all alike, all better than their parents, and be right about the eleventh before it is born. The two sides meet where the orchards run out into the flooded rows, and every argument in the delta ends up standing in that water.

records.value: Young come from the body that carried the join, never from the part added on. Every animal she ever worked was rooted in a mudheart — the one delta creature that takes with anything — so all her pairings were mudheart to mudheart, and the litters are mudheart litters carrying nothing of the graft. She was not beating the rule. She was pairing the only part of the animal that was never joined, because pigeons taught her to look at the parent and not the ornament. report.title: The Root Decides
report.domain: Grafting and breeding — joining a piece cut from one living thing onto another so the two grow as one. Whether it takes depends on how near kin they are; the join is always the weakest place; a new join needs a season and a keeper; the part underneath decides how big and how strong, the part added on decides what it does; and what is joined does not have young, because young come from the body, not from the graft.
report.inversion_text: The mentor is removed. Nobody teaches Sela the thing she is best at, because it is not a discipline yet and there is no one alive who has done it. What fills the hole is Halder Vone, the breeder who takes her into his own pens to prove her wrong, teaches her his craft properly and generously in the course of it, and corrects her at every step for reasons that have nothing to do with her good.

world.premise:
Sela Quen is twenty-two and spent four years on a rooftop in a river port breeding racing pigeons, because she liked it and there was nothing else to do up there. The hobby teaches exactly one thing: watch what a bird passes on to its young, not what the bird looks like standing in front of you.

Then she came downriver into the delta, where people join living things together. A grafter cuts a part off one animal and binds it onto another, and if the two are near enough kin it takes and grows: a hound with a second heart, a man with an arm that used to belong to a bear. How far apart the two can be is how a grafter is known — same flesh, then like flesh, then far flesh, and above those a handful of people alive who can join two things with no kinship at all. Sela is a like flesh, two steps up, and slower at it than most people her age.

Everything a grafter makes is barren. Joined creatures never have young, so a grafter's work dies when the grafter does, and the only people here who make anything that outlasts them are the breeders, who join nothing, and whose bodies refuse another creature's flesh so hard that a breeder's flat palm on a fresh join will open it up.

Sela's crosses have young. She does not know why yet. Halder Vone, the best breeder in the delta, has taken her into his own pens to prove she is lying — and if she turns out not to be, everything his family is rests on her being stopped.
