systems.name: Taking
systems.logic: A body will grow together with another living thing only if it takes that thing for near enough kin. The nearer the kin, the surer the hold; the further, the more of it sloughs away in the first season. Whatever is joined has one weak place forever, exactly where the two met. A new join knits over a season and only if somebody stays close enough to keep it warm, still and watched. The body underneath decides how big and how strong the whole thing is; the part added on decides what it can do. And nothing joined has young.
systems.interface: Palm to a fresh join and the join opens: refusal beats a take every time, and nothing a grafter makes has ever held on a breeder's body. Children are sorted at eight by pressing a scrap of another child's skin to the inside of a wrist for three days — it takes, or the wrist swells and goes hot — and afterwards you are on one side of the delta or the other for good. What a grafter can do that a breeder never will: put a dead thing's working part into a living body and have it working by morning. What a breeder can do that a grafter never will: make ten of something, all alike, all better than their parents, and be right about the eleventh before it is born. The two sides meet where the orchards run out into the flooded rows, and every argument in the delta ends up standing in that water.
systems.manifests_as: A bound line goes pale and tight and warm to the back of the hand, and the animal favours that side for a whole season.
systems.view_withholds: A grafter cannot tell from the outside whether a join will hold past the second year; only sitting with it will say.

criterion.evaluates: How far apart two living things can be and still be joined by this person and live.

ranks.visible_form: Nothing walks behind them. They carry a mudheart on a rope and it has three pale lines across its back from where they practised putting the same leg on twice.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A season of sleeping on a floor with a hand through the slats of a crate, not leaving, not travelling, while the thing inside it either knits or rots and takes your forearm's skin with it if it rots.
ranks.grants: Put back onto a body what came off that same body, the same day, and have it work: a hand, an ear, a slit throat closed. In a delta full of animals and blades, they are the reason people survive the morning.

ranks.visible_form: One animal walks beside them with a part that plainly began on another of its own kind — a hound with one white leg, a heavy grey body carrying a jaw that does not match it.
ranks.cost_to_reach: Making a join on a creature that will die if you get it wrong, and then keeping the ones you got wrong: your first bad animal is yours to feed for as long as it lives, and it lives a long time.
ranks.grants: Replace what is gone with a working part off a like creature — a heart, a lung, a leg, an eye — so somebody who should have died by evening is standing up by the end of the week.

ranks.visible_form: The animal behind them has something no animal of its kind was born with: wings on a hound, a heron's throat on a river dog, and people step off the path to let it past.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A mismatched join feeds back up your own arms while it knits — you feel the animal's pain, every night, for the season — and there is no way to do it asleep.
ranks.grants: Give a body something its whole kind has never had: breathe under water for an hour, see in the dark, fly badly but fly — on an animal, or on a person who asks for it.

ranks.visible_form: Something walks with them that has no name, because nothing like it has been made before, and the delta names it after them instead.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A thing that is kin to nothing does not accept a keeper either. It takes about a year of being bitten by your own work before it stops, and the scars are on both forearms where everyone can see them.
ranks.grants: Join what shares nothing — wood and blood, river and beast — and have it hold together for years: a living thing that never existed, that hunts for you, that outlives the argument you made it for.

ranks.visible_form: Their own body has parts on it that came off everything they ever made, and they take one off and put another on in front of people, in the time it takes to change a coat.
ranks.cost_to_reach: You work the joins on yourself, both hands, no help, awake for all of it, because nobody else can feel where your own weak places want to sit — and half of those who try it are found in the morning having opened at three of them at once.
ranks.grants: Carry any part of anything you have ever made, swap it at need, and be refused by none of it: an arm for the hour you need that arm, lungs for the hour you are under water, an eye for the dark.

rules.rule: Two living things grow together only if the body takes the other for near enough kin. The nearer the kin, the surer the hold; the further apart, the more of the join comes apart in the first season.

consequences.consequence: Nearly every made creature in the delta is a mudheart underneath, because a mudheart takes with almost anything, and so everything anybody makes is slow, heavy and mild by nature.
A delta family keeps a cousin animal in the yard for spare parts the way another country keeps a woodpile, and names it, and is fond of it.
A grafter behind a line puts men back together overnight, so fights in the delta run for weeks and are decided by who runs out of animals.

rules.manifests_as: She holds a hound's foreleg against a hound's shoulder for a count of thirty, feels nothing come back, and puts it down and says no.

rules.rule: Wherever two things were joined is where the thing will break, and it never stops being the weak place.

consequences.consequence: A killing in the delta is a flat hand laid on the right part of a neck by somebody who was invited into the room.
Where a house's people carry their joins is the first thing a rival house learns and the last thing anybody says out loud.
The delta dresses in high collars and long sleeves in a climate that does not want them, and calls it manners.

rules.manifests_as: He shrugs his sleeve down over his elbow before he goes into the room, without noticing he did it.

rules.rule: A new join knits over one season and only if somebody keeps it warm, keeps it still, and stays near enough to catch it going wrong.

consequences.consequence: Grafters do not travel between the flood and the dry, and everybody always knows exactly where any of them is.
You beat a grafter by making them go somewhere, and every summons in the delta is really that.
The one held day here is the morning the water turns, when every join made that year is either alive and shown, or carried down and given to the river.

rules.manifests_as: She sleeps on the floor beside a crate with her hand through the slats, and has done it for sixty nights, and will do it for thirty more.

rules.rule: Nothing joined has young. Put two made creatures together for as long as you like and the pen stays at two.

consequences.consequence: The breeders own everything that lasts, because every grafter's whole life's work stops when the grafter does.
A grafter builds each animal from nothing, one at a time, and there is never a second one of anything good.
A grafter is buried with the last thing they made, alive, because it has nowhere else to be.

rules.manifests_as: Two of his best in the same pen for a whole season, and at the end of it he counts two.

systems.name: The Line
systems.logic: Nothing joins. A creature is only ever itself, and the way to make it better is to choose which ones have young, and then choose again, over generations, keeping the line clean and killing most of what you make. A body that works this way refuses another creature's flesh absolutely, and that refusal reaches out through the hands.
systems.interface: A breeder cannot be mended by the only craft in the delta that mends people, so the strongest families here are also the most easily killed, and both sides have known it for a hundred years without either being able to do anything about it.
systems.manifests_as: A palm laid flat and held, a pale line under the fur going wet and dark, and the join letting go.
systems.hidden_personality: The breeders' whole authority rests on grafters not being able to make anything that lasts, and every one of them knows exactly how thin that is.

criterion.evaluates: Whether any one animal from a line can be swapped for any other from that line without anyone being able to tell.

rules.rule: A breeder's body takes nothing that is not its own, and the hands carry that refusal outward: a flat palm held on a fresh join, and the join opens.

consequences.consequence: A breeder stands at every gate where made animals are brought in, and the touch on the way through is the permission.
One breeder walking a line is worth more than the line, and both sides know which one to put an arrow in.
Breeders shake hands with the fingertips only, and the delta has decided this is arrogance rather than habit.

rules.manifests_as: She puts her palm on the hound's shoulder and keeps it there while she talks, and by the end of the sentence the leg is loose.

rules.rule: One animal proves nothing. You have made a thing only when any one of them can be swapped for any other and nobody alive can tell which.

consequences.consequence: Breeder families marry to lines rather than to people, and the delta's whole map of who owes what runs on it.
A breeder kills more of his own animals than he keeps and does it in front of his students on purpose.
Nothing in the delta is sold in ones; a buyer takes ten or is not serious.

rules.manifests_as: He walks the pen, points at four without slowing down, and by evening there are four fewer; he does not look up while it is done.

rules.rule: Nothing that came out of anybody else can be put into a breeder. A wound they cannot heal on their own is a wound they die of.

consequences.consequence: Breeders do not go to the front and both sides stopped pretending otherwise two generations ago.
A breeder's house is built with no stairs, no open water and no horses, and visitors think it is poverty.
A grafter lays a hand on a dying man as a blessing; done to a breeder it means nothing at all, and doing it anyway is the oldest insult here.

rules.manifests_as: He steps down into the boat with both hands out like a man twice his age, and everybody looks somewhere else.

capabilities.is_a: Handle two living things and know how near kin they are, and so whether a join between them will take.
capabilities.manifests_as: She holds a foreleg against a shoulder for a slow count, feels the warmth come up or not come up in her own palms, and says yes or no.
capabilities.costs: She has to have both animals in her hands at once, and one of them is usually the kind that bites.

capabilities.is_a: Bind a part cut off one living thing onto another so that the two grow as one.
capabilities.manifests_as: An hour of work with wet cloth and both thumbs, then a pale tight line that is warm to the back of the hand for a season.
capabilities.costs: A season within a night's walk of the crate: no travelling, no answering a summons, no leaving even for a day.

capabilities.is_a: Look at two animals and say what their young will be like, better than chance — because she watches what a parent passes on rather than what the parent looks like.
capabilities.manifests_as: She points at two mild unremarkable animals in a yard of better ones, and eighteen months later everybody understands why.
capabilities.costs: It only pays out in generations, so she has to keep everything she has ever paired alive and fed for years to find out whether she was right, and she does the killing of the rest herself.

capabilities.is_a: Split a healed join with a flat palm and a little patience.
capabilities.manifests_as: A hand held on a shoulder through a whole conversation, and then the animal's leg does not take weight.
capabilities.costs: It works only skin to skin, so it has to be done close, in company, by somebody everybody can see doing it.

capabilities.is_a: Keep a join from opening under somebody else's palm by holding it yourself from the other side.
capabilities.manifests_as: Two people with their hands on the same animal, neither talking, for as long as it takes one of them to give up.
capabilities.costs: Both her hands are on the animal, which means both her hands are not anywhere else, and she cannot move her feet.

capabilities.is_a: Wear on your own body a working part that came off something else, and take it off again.
capabilities.manifests_as: He rolls a sleeve down over one arm, works for an hour, and comes back with a different arm under the sleeve.
capabilities.costs: Every part worn is one more weak place on him, and the people who can open weak places know where all of his are.

cast.is_a: Twenty-two, from a river port upstream, four years of rooftop pigeons behind her and two steps up the delta's own reckoning of grafters.
cast.wants: To make a kind rather than a creature — something that goes on having young after she is gone.
cast.secret: Her first litter was an accident she did not notice for a month, and she has been pretending since day one that she knows what she did.
cast.false_belief: That the thing she can do is about her, and that Halder will eventually have to admit it.
cast.voice_tag: Talks about animals with total precision and about people with none.
cast.manifests_as: Feeding a long yard of misjoined animals at first light, naming every one of them, and drowning the two that cannot lift their heads.

relationships.note: She is standing in his pens, using his animals, being taught properly by a man who needs her to be wrong.
He told her that what she is doing is impossible, and then walked her to Halder's gate himself.
The first thing she ever made on a body she picked herself, and he will not be more than a room away.
Two years younger, already a far flesh, and correct that she is bad at the actual work.
Halder's daughter is the only person in the yard who wants Sela to be right, for reasons Sela has not worked out.

cast.is_a: The best breeder in the delta, fifty-eight, whose family's standing rests on nothing made ever lasting.
cast.wants: To find the mundane mistake in what Sela is doing, publicly, before anyone outside his yard hears about it.
cast.secret: His left hand is grafted. Wick put it on him when he was nine, before his own body learned to refuse, and he has carried a join through his entire career against everything he teaches.
cast.false_belief: That he will be able to stop at proving her wrong.
cast.prices_the_present: Every hour he spends teaching her properly is an hour she gets better, and he cannot bring himself to teach her badly.
cast.voice_tag: Precise, generous with knowledge, and absolutely cold about outcomes.
cast.manifests_as: Walking a pen, pointing at four, and going on with the sentence he was in the middle of.

relationships.note: He gave her the run of his pens, which is the most dangerous thing anyone has ever done for her.
The hand. Neither of them has mentioned it in forty years.
He wrote her down as a breeder at eight and has never once discussed it.
The line his family sells is the standard everything else in the delta is measured against.

cast.is_a: An old far flesh grafter, seventy-odd, who has not made anything new in sixty years and will not say why.
cast.wants: For the thing in the drowned orchard to die before he does.
cast.secret: He made the barkjaw, and he stopped the same week, and the reason he stopped is that it did not die when he asked it to.
cast.false_belief: That not teaching anybody the last step counts as having prevented anything.
cast.voice_tag: Answers a different question than the one asked, and the answer is usually the more useful one.
cast.manifests_as: Sitting on an upturned crate with his hands in his sleeves, telling somebody exactly what they did wrong an hour after it stopped mattering.

relationships.note: Everything she knows about joins, and he told her flat that made things do not breed.
Put a hand on a nine-year-old before anybody knew what that boy was going to grow into.
He goes out to the flooded rows twice a year and comes back without having gone in.

cast.is_a: Twenty, already a far flesh, the fastest pair of hands in the delta and the first grafter in three generations everyone expects to reach the far end.
cast.wants: To be the one who makes something with no kinship in it, before he is thirty, and to have it happen in front of people.
cast.secret: He has tried the no-kin join four times and buried all four, and he does the burying at night.
cast.false_belief: That Sela's litters are a trick and that finding the trick is beneath him.
cast.voice_tag: Friendly, quick, and steps on the end of other people's sentences.
cast.manifests_as: His hound comes into a room first, with wings folded badly along its back, and everybody looks at it and not at him.

relationships.note: He is better at the work and she has done the thing, and neither of them can get past that.
Wick will not teach him the last step and will not say why, and Tam has decided it is spite.

cast.is_a: Halder's daughter, nineteen, written down as a breeder at eight and living in a house full of people who would drown her work if she had any.
cast.wants: To be tested again, properly, in front of witnesses.
cast.secret: When they pressed the scrap to her wrist it neither took nor swelled. Nothing happened at all, and her father wrote breeder and closed the book.
cast.prices_the_present: She cannot lay a palm on a join and open it, and has spent eleven years covering for that with confidence.
cast.voice_tag: Understates everything, including things that should be shouted.
cast.manifests_as: Putting her hand on an animal and leaving it there a beat too long, hoping, and taking it back.

relationships.note: She knows he wrote something down that morning and she has never been allowed to see it.
Sela is the only person who has ever asked her what actually happened at eight.

institutions.is_a: Six hundred paces of clean dry pens on the high ground above the flood, where the delta's standard line of animals is made and most of it is killed.
institutions.wants: To be the thing every other animal in the delta is measured against for another hundred years.
institutions.secret: The line has been narrowing for a decade and this year's are worse than last year's, and Halder is the only one who has noticed.
institutions.reach: Every yard in the delta buys from here or copies from here.
institutions.recognises: Anybody who can be swapped for somebody else without a difference showing.
institutions.manifests_as: A long row of animals that are so alike a visitor keeps thinking they have walked back past the same one.

relationships.note: He is the line and the line is him, which is a problem neither survives.
She sleeps in a store shed at the end of the row and has the run of every pen.
Every grafter in the delta learned their trade in water the Vones have never stood in.

institutions.is_a: The grafters' side of the delta: crates on stilts, wet floors, and people sleeping with a hand through the slats from flood to dry.
institutions.wants: To make one thing that outlives the person who made it.
institutions.secret: Three of the yards have quietly agreed never to go into the flooded orchard rows again, and none of them told the fourth.
institutions.reach: Wherever somebody has been cut open and needs to be standing by morning.
institutions.manifests_as: A row of low sheds at the water line, and outside each one an animal that is not quite any animal you know.

relationships.note: They mend everybody and own nothing that lasts, and both halves of that are the same fact.
He is the oldest one left and the only one who ever went past far flesh.

institutions.is_a: The sorting: every child in the delta, at eight, with a scrap of another child's skin bound to the inside of the wrist for three days.
institutions.wants: Nothing. It is a morning that happens whether anybody wants it or not.
institutions.secret: About one child in two hundred does neither — no take, no swelling — and the delta has no word for it, so it writes down breeder and moves on.
institutions.recognises: A wrist that takes, or a wrist that swells and goes hot.
institutions.manifests_as: A line of children with their sleeves rolled, and on the third morning a table of adults going along the row lifting each arm and saying one word.

relationships.note: Her wrist did nothing, and her father was the man holding the pen.
She was eight upstream, on a roof, with pigeons, and nobody here has thought to ask.

agencies.is_a: The flood that comes up the delta once a year and goes down again, and decides what anybody is able to do in between.
agencies.wants: Nothing, and it takes what it wants anyway.
agencies.reach: Every join in the delta: a season is a season because the water says so.
agencies.recognises: Nothing. It comes up over the low yards whether the crates are ready or not.
agencies.false_belief: The delta's belief, not its own: that the turn is roughly the same date every year, which it has not been for six years.
agencies.prices_the_present: Every grafter's whole life is arranged around not being able to leave for one half of the year, and around having to leave for the other.
agencies.manifests_as: Brown water standing between the orchard rows, and boats tied to the tops of fences.
agencies.secret: It is coming up later and staying longer, which is slowly making the drowned orchard bigger and bringing the barkjaw's rows nearer to the low yards each year.

relationships.note: When the water turns, every join made that year is either alive and shown, or given to the river.
It has been widening the thing's country for six years.

carriers.is_a: A thumbnail of another child's skin, bound to the inside of an eight-year-old's wrist for three days.
carriers.grants: It says which side of the delta a person spends their life on, in one word, on the third morning.
carriers.manifests_as: A grubby strip of cloth on a small arm, and a queue of children comparing whose has started to itch.
carriers.secret: It reads whether a body refuses. It has never been able to read a body that simply does not care either way.

relationships.note: The whole sorting is one scrap of skin and three days, and nobody has ever proposed a better test.

history.is_a: The great made creatures of sixty and eighty years ago — the river-walkers, the tall things that carried whole families — every one of them dead now with the person who made it.
history.prices_the_present: The delta remembers what it used to have and cannot rebuild a single one, and every grafter grows up under that.
history.manifests_as: A carved post at the head of the low yards with the outlines of nine animals on it, none of which anybody living has seen.
history.secret: Two of the nine were not made. They bred, and the men who kept the record wrote them down as made, because the other answer would have handed the delta to the grafters.

relationships.note: Every grafter's ambition is a copy of a shape on a post.
The record was kept by a Vone.

creatures.is_a: A heavy, mild river animal about the size of a pig, which will take a join from almost anything.
creatures.mechanism: Its body barely distinguishes its own flesh from anybody else's, so a part bound to it knits inside a season and holds for years.
creatures.ecology: Root-feeders in the shallow channels, far too slow to live anywhere the water moves.
creatures.human_use: Nearly every made creature in the delta is a mudheart underneath with something else's parts on top, which is why everything anybody makes is placid.
creatures.behaviour: Stands where it is put, eats what is in front of it, and follows whoever fed it last.
creatures.manifests_as: A wide grey back with three or four pale lines across it, and something on it that obviously started life on another animal.
creatures.rank: The body under nearly everything, and the reason nobody here has ever asked what the body contributes.
creatures.bond_potential: It will attach itself permanently to one person on the strength of two meals, which the delta finds funny rather than useful.

creatures.is_a: Sela's first made animal: a mudheart body with a river hound's legs and a spearbill heron's throat and lungs.
creatures.mechanism: The heron parts hold air for a long stretch under water, the hound legs give the mudheart speed it was never born with, and the joins sit at both shoulders and at the base of the throat.
creatures.ecology: He can work the flooded orchard rows, which nothing else in the delta can do for more than a minute.
creatures.human_use: Sela makes joins under water in flood season by putting her mouth to his and taking the air he is holding.
creatures.behaviour: Will not be more than a room from her, and puts himself between her and any hand that comes at her flat and open.
creatures.manifests_as: A long grey throat that does not belong on a dog, and a breath held so long that strangers in the yard start counting out loud.
creatures.bond_potential: Already hers. He was the first thing she made on a body she chose herself, and he is the father of the litter nobody can explain.

creatures.is_a: A thing made sixty years ago out of wood and living flesh, still walking the drowned orchard rows.
creatures.mechanism: Nothing in it is kin to anything else in it, so all of it is weak places; it has learned to move so that no part of it takes weight for long, and in sixty years it has neither healed nor rotted.
creatures.ecology: Lives in the flooded rows and eats the trees, and its country gets bigger every year the water stays up longer.
creatures.human_use: None. Three of the four yards have quietly agreed not to go out there, and did not tell the fourth.
creatures.behaviour: Does not hunt. Takes apart anything that touches the trees, slowly, without hurrying, and stops the moment the thing stops moving.
creatures.manifests_as: A sound of wet wood bending, and a shape standing a head too tall for the row it is standing in.
creatures.rank: The only no-kin creature alive in the delta, and the reason there are no others.

bonds.joint_ability: She works a join under the flood water for as long as he can hold his breath, because every few minutes she puts her mouth to his and takes back the air he is storing — nobody else in the delta can make anything at all once the water is up.
bonds.trait_link: Both of them were made by somebody who chose the body first and worried about the parts afterwards.

mysteries.question: Which side did Pella Vone actually come out on at the wrist morning?
mysteries.answer: Neither. The scrap did not take and the wrist never swelled — nothing happened at all, which happens to about one child in two hundred and has no name here. Her father wrote breeder, closed the book, and has never spoken of it, which is why she cannot open a join and has spent eleven years covering for it.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: The whole Vone yard, who believe she is simply an indifferent breeder with a famous father.

mysteries.question: Who made the thing in the drowned orchard, and why did no one ever make another?
mysteries.answer: Wick made it, sixty years ago, at the far end of what anybody has reached. He stopped that same week — not because it turned on him, but because he asked it to lie down and die and it did neither, and he understood he had made something that did not need him and could not be taken back.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: The low yards, who think it wandered in from upriver.

mysteries.question: Why does Halder Vone never use his left hand for anything that matters?
mysteries.answer: It is not his. Wick put it on him at nine, before his own body learned to refuse, and he has carried a join through an entire career spent proving that joins are worthless. It is the one thing on him that his own craft says cannot be there, and it is exactly where anyone who knows would put a palm.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: The delta, which assumes an old injury and good manners.

mysteries.question: Why do Sela's made creatures have young when nothing made ever has?
mysteries.answer: Young come from the body that carried the join, never from the part added on. Every animal she ever worked was rooted in a mudheart — the one delta creature that takes with anything — so all her pairings were mudheart to mudheart, and the litters are mudheart litters carrying nothing of the graft. She was not beating the rule. She was pairing the only part of the animal that was never joined, because pigeons taught her to look at the parent and not the ornament. The rule stands exactly as written, and the real question, the one that runs the rest of the book, is whether anything of the added part can ever be got into the young.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Everyone, grafters and breeders alike, who judge a creature entirely by the part that was added on.

mysteries.question: What is past the far end, and why has nobody who reached it ever gone further?
mysteries.answer: Joining yourself: carrying parts of everything you have ever made, swappable, refused by none of it. Almost nobody does it because every part worn is one more weak place on your own body, in a delta where the strongest family alive opens weak places with an open hand.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Tam, who believes the far end is the end and that reaching it is the whole of it.

directives.text: Fast and plain, warm about animals, unsentimental about what happens to them. The engine is shown by hands doing work, never explained.
No technical vocabulary from the real craft ever reaches the page. The delta says take, join, root, top, throw young, same flesh, like flesh, far flesh, no kin, whole hand.

Every step up costs on the page in the same chapter or earlier: a season she cannot leave, an animal she has to keep forever, a night of feeling somebody else's pain through her hands, a person who is now against her.
The first twelve scenes get Sela from her own shed into Halder's pens, put a second litter on the page in front of witnesses, and settle the question of what happened to Pella at eight.
The showing — walking your animal out where people can see what is on it — is the world's set piece. Use one early and let the litter arrive in the middle of one.
